description: Ukraine's long-range drone strikes on Caspian Sea cargo vessels carrying Iranian military supplies mark a new phase in the convergence of the Russia-Ukraine war and the US-Iran confrontation. One Iranian sailor was killed, and Tehran threatens retaliation.

faqs.answer: Ukraine's SBU identified the targets as the cargo ship Port Olya 2 (IMO 9481881), the dry cargo ship Begey (IMO 8943210), and a Russian Project 12418 Molniya-class missile boat. Ukrainian drones also struck the Lukoil-operated Filanovsky field oil platform.
faqs.question: What vessels did Ukraine strike in the Caspian Sea?

faqs.answer: One Iranian sailor was killed and another was wounded. Iran has not released the name of the deceased. The vessel was reportedly hit on the bridge and damaged severely enough to require rescue by maritime authorities in Astrakhan, Russia.
faqs.question: Who was killed in the strike?

faqs.answer: The Khorramshahr-4 is an Iranian medium-range ballistic missile with an estimated range of 2,000 km and a warhead of approximately 1,500 kg. Pro-Iranian Telegram channels published maps showing that this range would cover all of Ukraine from Iranian territory, though Iran's government has not officially confirmed or denied this capability.
faqs.question: What is the Khorramshahr-4 missile?

faqs.answer: The Caspian is the primary maritime corridor linking Iran's northern ports (Bandar Anzali, Amirabad) to Russian ports (Astrakhan, Makhachkala, Kaspiysk). Russia received its first batches of Iranian Shahed drones via the Caspian, and the route continues to carry drone components, missile parts, and Fatah-360 launchers. With US pressure on Iran's southern coast, the Caspian is now Iran's last secure heavy-cargo trade route.
faqs.question: Why does the Caspian Sea matter for the Russia-Iran military supply chain?

leadParagraph: On July 25, Ukrainian forces conducted long-range drone strikes against cargo ships carrying Iranian military supplies and a Russian warship in the Caspian Sea, killing one Iranian sailor and wounding another. Iran's foreign minister warned the attack 'cannot go unanswered,' and pro-Iranian channels published maps showing all of Ukraine within range of Iranian ballistic missiles. The strike exposes the deepening military alliance between Russia and Iran — and the merging of two wars that were once treated as separate conflicts.

methodology: This article draws on official statements from Ukraine's Security Service (SBU), Iran's Ministry of Foreign Affairs (IRNA), Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky's public addresses, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi's X posts, reporting by the Guardian, CNBC, Newsweek, the Kyiv Post, the Jerusalem Post, Maritime Executive, Marine Insight, and The Week. Vessel identification relies on IMO registry data and Ukrainian military intelligence records. Missile range data is based on publicly available specifications for the Khorramshahr-4 system. Historical Caspian shipping route analysis draws on open-source maritime tracking and documented satellite imagery.
title: Ukraine Strikes Iranian Military Vessel in Caspian Sea — One Sailor Killed, Tehran Threatens Retaliation
